correctness.rationale: At each prefix the strongest EFX inequality against the higher-valued rival deletes its smallest good. For positive alpha, first-day H,L must be split. Up to agent symmetry there are precisely four day-two allocations: crossing yields cap C=(H+2L)/(2H) even after checking both day-three goods to one agent; repeating gives 2L/H<=C when H>=2L; both to the initially high recipient gives L/(2H)<=C; both to the other recipient yields D=H/(H+L). Explicit 3-day schedules attain C and D without early prefix violations. An alternating high/low assignment attains exact EFX at every horizon precisely when H<=2L; the day-3 upper bound excludes exact EFX for H>2L for all T>=3. C decreases and D increases on h>2; their crossing solves h²-3h-2=0 and yields the stated sharp minimum. Independently enumerated all 64 three-day labeled schedules with rational arithmetic at 10 ratios including branch boundaries; symbolic case proof handles real h and all T.

originality.rationale: Choi and Li 2026 primary papers establish general impossibility even for identical days and two agents, a 1/2-TEFX constructive guarantee for that broader class, and L/H approximation under bi-valued goods. Their exact witness uses three goods per day including zero, whereas this theorem restricts to two strictly positive goods recurring daily and computes the sharp ratio-dependent three-day optimum. Full accessible arXiv HTML for the 2607 paper was inspected in relevant Sections 4,5,6 and appendices: Theorem 4.2 is a lower guarantee, Theorems 5.1 and 6.1 are general input-class lower guarantees whose global tightness witnesses do not force a matching upper bound in this strict subfamily. The submitted entire two-branch frontier is not implied by the general results; priority is qualified.
residual_risks: Originality is best-knowledge; specialized unpublished exact two-item repeated TEFX bounds may exist.

value.rationale: The first obstructed horizon and exact H/L=2 existence boundary are natural structure parameters in repeated allocation, and the nontrivial switch between splitting and assigning both goods to one agent produces an exact tight two-branch policy frontier. This resolves a meaningful constrained fair-division question rather than merely restating the prior 1/2 guarantee or negative instance.

limitations: Two agents with identical additive preferences, exactly one H and L each day, goods never reallocated, cumulative EFX at every prefix. Approximate factor only classified through T=3; for T>3 exact feasibility only.
